text:
Nina: Quick note  spotted a small but confusing line in Optimize toolkit batching docs: we recommend "small-batch" for short sequences but the example YAML uses batch_size: 64 which is large for short seqs. I pushed a tiny PR to adjust examples and add a short/long example split: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4920 :eyes:
Marco: Good catch. Which files changed?
Nina: /optimize/batching/rules.md and examples/snippets/batching.yaml. I split the YAML into two named profiles: short-seq (batch_size: 8, max_tokens: 64) and long-seq (batch_size: 64, max_tokens: 4096).
Priya: Can you add a note about latency tradeoffs and an example measuring p50? A single line with expected p50 delta would help readers calibrate.
Nina: Added a table row: "short-seq: lower cost, lower throughput; p50 ~ 20-40ms on rwr/small; long-seq: higher throughput, p50 ~ 120-250ms" — rough numbers with a callout to bench results.
Marco: Also add a cross-link to /optimize/quant/profiles.md noting q_profile recommendations for short vs long sequences.
Nina: Done. Also fixed a stale link to examples/old-batching.md and added a redirect.
DocsBot: PR 4920 opened by Nina; reviewers: Marco, Priya. Docs CI: link-check queued.
Priya: Reviewing now, will comment if any wording tweaks. Small ask: mention that batch_size values assume KV prefetch enabled for long sequences.
Nina: Good point, added that sentence. Aim to merge by EOD. Thanks.
